name: Bhujangasana
description: A prone backbend. Lying face down, the chest lifts away from the floor with the hips and legs grounded, elbows staying soft and shoulders drawing back and down. Best assessed from a side view.
camera_hint: Place your camera to your side, about 2-3 metres away, so your whole body is in frame from the side.
image_credit: Photo: Kennguru / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
benefits: Mobilises the thoracic spine into extension
Opens the chest and the front of the shoulders
Gently strengthens the muscles along the spine
cues: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders
Press the tops of your feet and your hips into the floor
Lift your chest by lengthening forward and up, not by pushing hard with the arms
Keep a soft bend in your elbows
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears

feedback.low: You are arching too sharply. Lengthen forward through the crown of your head to spread the curve along the whole spine.
feedback.high: Lift your chest further to bring your spine into a gentle backbend.

feedback.low: Lift your chest higher away from the floor while keeping your hips grounded.
Keep your hips pressing down into the floor.
feedback.high: Your hips are lifting off the floor. Lower them and lift through the chest instead.

feedback.low: Press a little more through your hands to lift the chest.
feedback.high: Soften your elbows. Keep a slight bend rather than locking the arms straight.

feedback.low: Press a little more through your hands to lift the chest.
feedback.high: Soften your elbows. Keep a slight bend rather than locking the arms straight.

feedback.low: Straighten your legs and press the tops of your feet into the floor.
Straighten your legs and press the tops of your feet into the floor.
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears and broaden across the collarbones.
You are too upright for Cobra. Lie down on your front with your hips on the floor.
